categories.main_business_segments: Kewell Technology Co., Ltd. operates primarily in three business segments: testing power supplies, hydrogen energy testing and intelligent manufacturing equipment, and power semiconductor testing and intelligent manufacturing equipment. These segments serve industries such as new energy power generation, electric vehicles, fuel cells and electrolyzers, and power semiconductors. The company also extends its products to sectors like rail transit, automotive electronics, intelligent manufacturing, electromechanical equipment, aerospace, and laboratory certification.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core technologies include power electronics conversion technologies such as AC/DC rectification, DC/AC inversion, and DC/DC chopper technologies. It has proprietary innovations like high dynamic multi-BUCK conversion, low harmonic PWM grid-feeding technology, high-voltage cascaded multi-level conversion, multi-CPU parallel control, and modular high-reliability power units. The company also develops precision measurement and control technologies, fuel cell testing calibration, and semiconductor device testing technologies, including SiC device testing. Production methods emphasize standardization, modular design, and platform-based development to improve efficiency and product quality.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Kewell serves key customers in the new energy power generation sector (notably photovoltaic and energy storage systems), electric vehicle manufacturers (covering motors, controllers, and batteries), hydrogen energy companies (fuel cell and electrolyzer testing), and power semiconductor manufacturers. Major customers include State Power Investment Corporation, Dongfang Electric (Chengdu) Hydrogen Fuel Cell Technology Co., Ltd., and Hangzhou Weidan Electronics Co., Ltd. The company’s products support R&D, production line testing, and quality inspection in these industries.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company primarily operates within China, with significant sales concentrated domestically across major economic regions. It has established subsidiaries and offices in cities including Hefei, Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, Xi’an, and Chongqing. Internationally, it has a wholly-owned subsidiary in the Netherlands (KEWELL EUROPE B.V.) focused on sales and import-export activities. Overseas sales are a smaller portion but growing, with efforts to expand global marketing and service networks.
categories.supply_chain_position: Kewell operates mainly in the midstream segment of the supply chain as a manufacturer and supplier of testing power supplies, testing systems, and intelligent manufacturing equipment. It provides critical testing and quality assurance tools to downstream manufacturers in new energy, automotive, hydrogen, and semiconductor sectors. The company also engages in upstream R&D and collaborates with suppliers for key components, focusing on supply chain security and domestic substitution of critical materials.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic focus is on expanding product series and standardization in testing power supplies, deepening capabilities in hydrogen energy and power semiconductor testing, and developing integrated testing solutions. R&D priorities include high-frequency DC power supplies, high-precision bidirectional AC/DC power supplies, SiC device testing, fuel cell and electrolyzer testing platforms, and automation in semiconductor packaging. It emphasizes platform-based development, modular design, and collaboration with universities and key customers to accelerate innovation and shorten development cycles.
categories.revenue_model: Kewell generates revenue primarily through the sale of testing power supplies, testing systems, and intelligent manufacturing equipment. Sales are conducted mainly via direct sales complemented by an expanding distribution network, especially for standardized small-power products. Revenue streams include product sales, technical services, equipment leasing, and after-sales support. The company also benefits from government subsidies related to technology and innovation.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Kewell is positioned as a leading domestic testing power supply and equipment manufacturer in China, with growing market share in new energy, electric vehicles, hydrogen energy, and power semiconductors. It competes with international giants like Keysight Technologies, Ametek, Thermo Fisher, and specialized firms such as Greenlight, FuelCon, and Chroma. The company has achieved import substitution in large-power testing power supplies and is advancing in small-power segments against Taiwanese and other foreign brands. It is recognized for its comprehensive product lines and technological innovation.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2023, Kewell reported revenue of approximately RMB 529 million, a 41% increase year-over-year, and net profit attributable to shareholders of RMB 117 million, up 88%. The company’s total assets grew by 27% to RMB 1.73 billion, with net assets increasing 27% to RMB 1.31 billion. R&D investment was RMB 82 million, accounting for 15.56% of revenue. The company has shown strong growth driven by expanding product lines and market demand in its core industries.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Kewell emphasizes its comprehensive and integrated testing solutions based on advanced power electronics technology, offering high reliability, precision, and efficiency. Its products support critical testing needs in emerging strategic industries like new energy, electric vehicles, hydrogen, and semiconductors. The company differentiates itself through proprietary core technologies, modular and standardized product design, strong R&D capabilities, and localized manufacturing that enables competitive pricing and faster delivery. It also provides robust after-sales service and collaborates closely with leading customers to tailor solutions.
